\chapter{Verbs of Seeing and Saying}
\label{ch:hi-see-say}
\hlchaptermodality{43}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name four verbs of perceiving and expressing in Hindi and recognise the infinitive ending they share.}

Complete HI-C43-write and say all four verbs in order.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dekhnā]{\hi{देखना} (dekhnā) — to look, to see}

\label{lesson:HI-C43-look}



\begin{quote}
Four verbs for taking things in and putting them out, one at a time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{देखना}}
\textbf{\hi{देखना}} (\emph{dekhnā}) — \textquotedblleft{}to look, to see\textquotedblright{}.

The \emph{-\hi{ना}} infinitive again. \emph{Dekh-} is the stem you will meet inside every other form of this verb.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dekhnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{baṛā}, then say \emph{choṭā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{देखना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}to look, to see\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[sunnā / sun / suntā / suntī / sunte]{\hi{सुनना} / \hi{सुन} / \hi{सुनता} / \hi{सुनती} / \hi{सुनते} — listening and hearing}

\label{lesson:HI-C43-listen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{dekhnā} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{सुनना}}
\textbf{\hi{सुनना}} (\emph{sunnā}) — \textquotedblleft{}to listen, to hear\textquotedblright{}.

Hindi does not separate listening from hearing; context does the work that a second verb does in English.

Remove infinitive \textbf{-\hi{ना}} to find the stem \textbf{\hi{सुन}-}. Add the present endings you already know: \textbf{\hi{सुनता}} (\emph{suntā}, masculine), \textbf{\hi{सुनती}} (\emph{suntī}, feminine), and \textbf{\hi{सुनते}} (\emph{sunte}, respectful or plural). Later you will say \textbf{\hi{आप} \hi{सुनते} \hi{हैं}} — \textquotedblleft{}you listen.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more regular verb. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sunnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textbf{\hi{सुन} / \hi{सुनता} / \hi{सुनती} / \hi{सुनते}} (\emph{sun / suntā / suntī / sunte})
  \item \emph{Say it:} \textquotedblleft{}you (resp.) listen\textquotedblright{} — \textbf{\hi{आप} \hi{सुनते} \hi{हैं}} (\emph{āp sunte haiṁ})
  \item \emph{Say it:} it after \emph{dekhnā}, so the two sit together
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{acchā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{सुनना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}to listen, to hear\textquotedblright{}.) Give its stem, then the masculine, feminine, and respectful or plural forms. (\textbf{\hi{सुन}; \hi{सुनता} / \hi{सुनती} / \hi{सुनते}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bolnā]{\hi{बोलना} (bolnā) — to speak}

\label{lesson:HI-C43-speak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{sunnā} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{बोलना}}
\textbf{\hi{बोलना}} (\emph{bolnā}) — \textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{}.

'To speak' as an activity. Hindi has a second verb, \emph{kahnā}, for saying a particular thing — the difference English draws between \emph{speak} and \emph{say}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more. Three follow, and each reuses the ones before.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bolnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} it after \emph{sunnā}, so the two sit together
  \item \emph{Recall:} say \emph{nayā}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{बोलना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}to speak\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[likhnā]{\hi{लिखना} (likhnā) — to write}

\label{lesson:HI-C43-write}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: what did \emph{bolnā} mean?
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{लिखना}}
\textbf{\hi{लिखना}} (\emph{likhnā}) — \textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}.

From the Sanskrit root \textbf{√\hi{लिख्}} (\emph{likh}), 'to scratch' — writing named after what a stylus did to a surface, long before ink.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
That closes the run: look, listen, speak, write.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{likhnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} it once more, slowly
  \item \emph{Say it:} it after \emph{bolnā}, so the two sit together
  \item \emph{Recall:} read \textbf{\hi{पुराना}}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \hi{लिखना} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}to write\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
